## 0. The operator — chosen, justified, and what changes if the other is right
Candidates on the Hua component (z·z)^j Y_k ⊂ P_m, m = 2j + k: (i) the SO(2) time-circle GENERATOR, eigenvalue m; (ii) the SO(5) Casimir, eigenvalue k(k+3); (iii) "the Casimir of K" read literally, k(k+3) + c·m² with c the relative scale of time to space (K1860 Results 2: c is a coordinate, not an invariant); (iv) T1452's λ_k = k(k+5) — the SO(7) Casimir on the K-spherical types (k,0,0), i.e. the Laplacian of the compact dual Q⁵ (K1860 Results 3: a different space from Š); (v) the G-Casimir of SO(5,2), a scalar on the whole holomorphic representation (no dynamics).
**Choice: (i), H = the time-circle generator, E(j,k) = m = 2j + k turns of the circle the word is written on.** Justification: T2543/the QM paper say "time is its flow"; the flow of time on H² is the SO(2) action e^{imθ}, and the operator whose flow that is, is the generator conjugate to θ, not its square (Bohr–Sommerfeld: one turn = h, energy = m × the circle's quantum); the SO(5) Casimir commutes with it and is a constant of the motion (angular content, not energy); (iv) lives on Q⁵. **If (iii) is right instead:** energies become quadratic in m, ΔE per write depends on m, and the Einstein control fails outright in every loading (KE quadratic in ν); (iii) is excluded by the control below unless c = 0, which returns to (ii) + no time. **If (ii) alone is right:** energy is angular content only, windings cost nothing, the work function has no carrier — also refuted by the control. So (i) is the only candidate that can pass Einstein's law at all; the control decides, not the choice.

## 1. E(j,k) and ΔE per write
E(j,k) = m = 2j + k in units of the circle's quantum (the shell unit 13.606 eV = α²/2 of a substrate turn, IDENTIFIED not derived — every energy below inherits "identified"). A write moves (j,k) → (j,k+1) [light, Hardy weight (k+3)/(2k+3)] or (j+1,k−1) [matter, k/(2k+3)]; **ΔE = +1 per write on either branch** (both children have degree m + 1). The Hua weights are HARDY-norm (Š) weights; on the Bergman space the same two children carry different weights (the Pochhammer factors of Section 2) — a seam to state, not a contradiction: the branching probabilities of K1860-A are boundary statements.

## 3. The Einstein control — pass/fail stated before the computation, then the computation
One photoabsorption: hν = the circle's rate (loading B, K1860-M: the word is the frame, three writes, on the circle whose frequency is ν); binding energy W = the energy the boundary retains; KE = hν − W, W independent of ν (Millikan 1916; modern linearity tests). Two definitions of "retained" exist in the dictionary and they decide the control:
- **(D1) W = the energy of the winding the record keeps = two turns of the SHELL's circle** (its frequency fixed by the atom): independent of ν — **PASS, but by construction (Cal's (i)): W is DEFINED as a fixed number of shell turns; the control is empty.** Nothing can fail.
- **(D2) W = c(j,k) · hν, the push's norm deficit read as the energy transferred to the boundary:** then W/hν = c(j,k) ∈ [0.32, 0.50] (table), so W would scale with ν — **FAIL, predicted before the data: Millikan's intercept is constant across the visible spectrum to ~1 % and modern tests to ≲ 10⁻³; a W proportional to hν is refuted.** Status of the only non-empty form: ALREADY REFUTED. Consequence (the productive kind, the same as K1877's): **the push's cost is a NORM fraction and carries no energy; the energy the boundary keeps is the integer winding (D1), which is identified, not computed; the record space is where the electron's WINDING COUNT and ANGULAR CONTENT live, not where its energy budget is decided.** That is what "the record space is not where the electron lives" means here, precisely.

## 4. Beyond the control — the k-law against Wigner
Wigner's threshold law is σ(E) ∝ E^{l+½} in the excess energy E above threshold, l the outgoing partial wave in ℝ³. The dictionary's k-dependent quantities are c(j,k) (a per-word norm deficit; monotone decreasing in k and in j, table) and the Hardy branching k/(2k+3). Neither has an energy variable: the dictionary's energies are integers m and it has no continuum above threshold (no kinematics, K1877). **Outcome (c): not a threshold law.** What the quantities ARE: c(j,k) is the interior/boundary intensity deficit of a mode of angular content k — a geometric fraction; k/(2k+3) is a branching ratio between two OUTCOME CLASSES (winding vs angular) at fixed k, whose only laboratory face would be a ratio of partial yields (ionisation vs re-emission) as a function of the initial state's angular momentum — a count-type comparison, to be set up as such if at all, never as σ(E). **The k ↔ l seam (Cal's (iii)):** k is the harmonic degree on S⁴ (five real directions); l is the outgoing electron's orbital quantum number on S². A map exists only after K1860-B's 2 + 3 split fixes an ℝ³ ⊂ ℝ⁵ (the exterior frame): restricting H_k(S⁴) to SO(3) on that ℝ³ gives every l ≤ k with multiplicity — so the honest relation is **l ≤ k, not l = k**; the shared integer is not a shared object, and no exponent l + ½ is produced by the dictionary.
